paras: The Bristol State Street disturbance was a confrontation on State Street in Bristol, Virginia, on the afternoon of Saturday, August 22, 1903, in which a white crowd cried "shoot" and "lynch" at two Black men. No one was reported killed, and the two men were "quickly hustled away to prevent violence"; a Richmond paper reported the incident under the headline "A Race Riot Was Imminent."

According to a special dispatch from Bristol dated August 24, a Black man pushed "a lady" off the sidewalk on State Street, and one of several white men who saw it "took the lady's part" and struck him. The correspondent wrote that a second Black man came to the first man's aid and that both drew knives, following the white man with "open knives" when he crossed the street "to arm himself." By then a "considerable crowd" had gathered, with cries of "shoot" and "lynch."
The two men were then hustled away, though the report does not say by whom or where they were taken.
No report of an arrest, charge or further violence appears in the coverage, and none of the people involved is named.

The only account found is the special dispatch printed on page 6 of The Times-Dispatch of Richmond on August 25, 1903. Its headline framed the incident as a near "race riot," and the text presented the push and the knife-drawing as fact, calling the first man "burley, insolent" and the second "dangerous-looking." The dispatch described the white man's blow as taking "the lady's part" and gave no account from the Black men.
No coverage of the incident was found in the Black press or in other white papers.

reader.title: Bristol State Street disturbance (1903)
bases: A crowd gathered and cried 'shoot' and 'lynch' at two Black men after a street altercation, but no one was seized, and the men were taken away before any further violence (A1).

No one was killed; a 'considerable crowd' threatened lynching over an alleged racial offense (pushing a white woman off the sidewalk), but the two Black men were 'hustled away to prevent violence' (A1).
The only report found is one special dispatch from Bristol to the Richmond Times-Dispatch (A1); no other white or Black paper carrying it was found.

accounts.label: Bristol correspondent of the Times-Dispatch
accounts.gist: A Black man pushed a white woman off the sidewalk, was struck by a white man, and with a companion drew knives and followed the white man; a crowd cried 'shoot' and 'lynch' before the Black men were hustled away.

framing.detail: Headlined 'A RACE RIOT WAS IMMINENT'; presents the sidewalk push and knife-drawing as fact, calls the men 'insolent' and 'dangerous-looking', and describes the blow as taking 'the lady's part'.

info: Saturday afternoon, August 22, 1903 (dispatch dated Aug. 24 says 'Saturday afternoon')
Two unnamed Black men: one accused of pushing a white woman off the sidewalk, and a second who came to his aid
Accused of pushing 'a lady' off the sidewalk; both men then said to have drawn knives and followed a white man across the street
A white man who struck the first Black man, and a 'considerable crowd' that cried 'shoot' and 'lynch'

sources.note: Special dispatch from Bristol, Va., Aug. 24, 'A RACE RIOT WAS IMMINENT': alleged sidewalk push on State Street Saturday, white man struck the Black man, knives drawn, crowd cried 'shoot,' 'lynch'; the Black men hustled away.
quotes: What came near resulting in a race riot happened on State Street, this city, Saturday afternoon.
A burley, insolent negro man pushed a lady off the sidewalk.
By this time a considerable crowd had gathered, and there were cries of "shoot," "lynch."
The negroes were quickly hustled away to prevent violence.
